overview: DOC AI is an AI-powered office documentation and deadline tracker. It helps teams process documents faster by combining OCR with prompt-engineering so key dates and deadlines surface automatically.
overviewExtra: Built as a React.js frontend with a Flask backend, the product focuses on workflow efficiency — turning messy docs into actionable tracking instead of manual follow-ups.
featuresIntro: The platform centers on smart extraction and a clean UI for day-to-day document work:
features: OCR-based document processing for scanned and uploaded files
ChatGPT prompt-engineering to extract key deadlines from content
React.js frontend for managing documents and tracking deadlines
Flask API integration for backend processing and workflow support

challenges.title: Reliable deadline extraction
challenges.body: Documents vary wildly in format. Tuning OCR output and prompts so deadlines stay accurate across different layouts was a core challenge.

conclusion: DOC AI reinforced how frontend UX and AI pipelines meet in real products — and how careful prompting plus OCR can cut repetitive office work.

overview: The Keycard Project is a role-based employee management system with Admin and Security panels. It streamlines ID creation and on-site verification with QR codes.
overviewExtra: Admins add employees, generate unique IDs with QR codes, and upload photos via Cloudinary. Security staff scan QR codes to verify details stored in MongoDB.
featuresIntro: Built for two clear roles — administration and security verification:
features: Admin panel to add employees and manage records
Auto-generated unique IDs with QR codes
Security panel for instant QR-based employee verification
MongoDB + Node.js/Express backend for storage and APIs

challenges.title: Role-based access clarity
challenges.body: Separating Admin and Security flows cleanly — without leaking privileges — required careful API and UI boundaries.

conclusion: Keycard showed how a focused full-stack tool can replace paper badges with a fast, scannable verification loop.

overview: A Medium-like blogging platform where users create and publish rich-text posts, follow others, explore trending articles, and engage with likes and comments.
overviewExtra: Appwrite powers authentication, database, and storage so the app stays focused on writing and community features without a custom auth stack.
featuresIntro: Core blogging and social loops included:
features: Follow other users and browse feeds

challenges.title: Content and auth with BaaS
challenges.body: Modeling posts, follows, and engagement on Appwrite while keeping the UI responsive took iteration on collections and permissions.

conclusion: The blog platform was a strong exercise in product-shaped full-stack work — publishing UX plus a managed backend.

project_name: AI-Based Adaptive Learning Platform for Children with Disabilities
overview: An AI-driven learning platform for children with disabilities, featuring real-time emotion detection, stress intervention, and interactive letter practice.
overviewExtra: The experience pairs a responsive frontend with API integration so learning moments adapt when a child shows stress or disengagement.
features: Stress intervention cues when learners need support
Flask APIs and MongoDB for backend data

challenges.title: Emotion detection in real time
challenges.body: Keeping OpenCV detection responsive in the browser/API loop while remaining gentle and useful for learners required careful UX and performance trade-offs.

conclusion: This project connected AI perception with inclusive education — building features that adapt to how a child feels, not only what they click.
